analysis.file_name: RBC November 22, 2026 Natural Gas Navigator A Grind From Here- 2027 update and 2028 rollout.pdf
analysis.title: Natural Gas Navigator: A Grind From Here, 2027 update and 2028 rollout
key_insights: RBC marked Q4 2026 Henry Hub to $3.15/MMBtu, lowered 2027 to $3.45/MMBtu and launched 2028 at $3.83/MMBtu. The path is a grind higher driven by demand-pull from LNG exports and power burn.

A super El Niño, now strong-to-very strong through January-March 2027 (79% probability per NOAA), sets up a mild withdrawal season. November HDDs are tracking about 6% below normal and December slightly below the 10-year average.

Production growth forecast is 3 Bcf/d y/y in 2027, led by Permian associated gas (2.3-2.6 Bcf/d y/y growth) and the Haynesville (about 1.9 Bcf/d each year). Lower-48 dry gas is forecast at 114.0 Bcf/d in 2027 and 118.7 Bcf/d in 2028.
New LNG export capacity of 6.2 Bcf/d in 2027 and 1.4 Bcf/d in 2028 is the clearest driver. Feedgas is forecast at 21.6 Bcf/d in 2027 and 24.9 Bcf/d in 2028, trending toward 30 Bcf/d by 2030.
Power burn forecast for 2028 is above 38 Bcf/d (38.8 in the balance), with about 70% of 2028 y/y growth tied to data centers. Nearly 30 GW of gas-fired capacity is planned over two years.

US midterm results add downside risk to data center gas burn. Democrats won key races in Texas, Ohio and Georgia, and Texas has 57 GW of behind-the-meter gas applications with only 36% finally approved, leaving 36.4 GW pending.

Democratic control of Congress adds uncertainty to EPA methane deregulation and permitting reform. The Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act 62-33, but House action before year-end is uncertain.

Iran war, nearly nine months in, has lifted TTF 158% and Asian spot 189% since the start while Henry Hub is relatively unchanged. US LNG exports rose 20% y/y in the first three quarters, with Asia up 105% and Europe down 6% for March-September.

Europe enters winter with storage 75% full versus a 5-year average of 89%, and Germany at 58% versus 88%. Europe is a price taker, so low storage could keep demand elevated even if Qatari supply recovers.
Managed money positioning has weakened significantly, leaving the market exposed to a sharp rally on unexpected cold. CTA short covering could reinforce a weather-driven move.
RBC's outlook sits slightly above the curve and above consensus median for 2027, and roughly in line with consensus for 2028. RBC says it is cautious about getting overly bearish.
Volatility is currently in line with historical averages and may not meet usual withdrawal-season hype absent large cold spells. RBC leans mildly toward a 2024-style end to the year over 2023.
Storage: 2028 end-of-season storage is forecast closer to 2022 levels (end of withdrawal 1.5 Tcf, end of injection 3.7 Tcf). The 2028 risk skew is incrementally higher than 2027.

sector_views.rationale: Demand-pull from LNG exports and power burn tightens the balance into H2 2027 and 2028, though near-term prices are weighed down by a mild El Niño winter.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Marked to market for weak weather, with neutral risk for the early withdrawal season.
Lowered, with downside risk in H1 and upside risk in H2 as LNG capacity arrives.
New base case with upside risk, low scenario $3.44 and high scenario $5.36.

macro_indicators.indicator: NOAA strong-to-very strong El Niño probability
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports a warmer lower-48 winter and weaker rescomm demand.
Export demand is absorbing supply, with Asia the main destination.

risk_factors: Cold snaps during an El Niño winter could cause short-duration volatility and a short-covering rally.
Data center gas burn downside from stricter state policies, plus behind-the-meter demand that may not show up in power data.
Starting oversupplied balance and weak withdrawal season weigh on H1 2027 prices.
Congressional gridlock could stall permitting reform and challenge EPA deregulation.
LNG utilization may fall in 2028 as capacity grows, and Middle East supply recovery would change global flows.
charts_described: Table in the report shows RBC Henry Hub scenarios for 2027: low $3.11, middle $3.45, high $4.59, and for 2028: low $3.44, middle $3.83, high $5.36.
vol_and_positioning: Managed money positioning has weakened significantly, leaving the market exposed to a sharp rally on unexpected cold and possible CTA short covering.
Historical volatility is in line with long-term average levels and RBC sees this withdrawal season as a potential end to the higher-intra-seasonal-vol trend.
Early 2026 saw a volatility spike, but the year otherwise bucked the multi-year pattern of higher volatility in later years.
geopolitical: Iran war nearly nine months old with limited prospects for a lasting ceasefire, disrupting Middle East gas supply and straining global LNG markets.
Loss of Qatari supply pulled US LNG toward Asia, with USGC-to-Asia netbacks above Europe from March to September.
US midterm outcomes and Democratic control of Congress create policy uncertainty for data center permitting, EPA methane rules and permitting reform.

tension_points.bull_case: Power burn above 38 Bcf/d in 2028 with about 70% of y/y growth from data centers, and nearly 30 GW of new gas generation planned.
tension_points.bear_case: Midterm wins by candidates favoring stricter development rules could delay Texas permits, and behind-the-meter demand may not show in power data.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Extension of Texas's existing air-permit pause under Governor-elect Hinojosa, or failure of permitting reform in the House before year-end.

theme_stances.key_argument: LNG export capacity growth and power demand call on supply, outpacing production growth and lifting prices through 2028 despite a weak near-term winter.
theme_stances.evidence: this all still represents a grind higher driven by the demand-pull dynamic

theme_stances.key_argument: A super El Niño sets the tone for a mild withdrawal season with HDDs below the 10-year average.
theme_stances.evidence: A super El Niño presents the biggest weather risk this winter
